title: Norm Equations in Number Fields of Degree > 2

problemStatement.formal: For a number field $K$ of degree $n=r_1+2r_2>2$, describe the solutions $\xi\in\mathcal{O}_K$ of the norm equation $N_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\xi)=m$. For $m=1$ this is the unit equation, governed by Dirichlet: $\mathcal{O}_K^\times\cong\mu_K\times\mathbb{Z}^{r_1+r_2-1}$; for general $m$, solutions split into finitely many $\mathcal{O}_K^\times$-orbits. The classical Pell equation $x^2-Dy^2=1$ is the case $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt D)$ (signature $(2,0)$, rank $1$).
problemStatement.plain: Generalize Pell beyond quadratics: in a cubic-or-higher number field the norm-one units have rank r1+r2-1 (so possibly several fundamental units), and N(xi)=m has finitely many solution classes modulo units.
whyMatters: Bridges the gallery’s concrete Pell entry to the structural heart of algebraic number theory (Dirichlet unit theorem, regulators, S-unit finiteness).
The deep core (Dirichlet) is already in Mathlib; the work is specialization + packaging, a high-value formalization.

proven: Signature/rank computed from first principles for 5 fields (sympy-verified): Q(sqrt2)=(2,0) rank1; Q(sqrt-5)=(0,1) rank0; Q(cbrt2)=(1,1) rank1; x^3-3x-1 totally real=(3,0) rank2; Q(zeta5)=(0,2) rank1. Identity r1+2r2=n holds in all.
Cubic norm form N(a+b t+c t^2)=a^3+2b^3+4c^3-6abc for Q(cbrt2) DERIVED as det of the multiplication-by-xi matrix on the power basis (not assumed).
Fundamental unit of Z[cbrt2]: u=t-1 with N(u)=1, inverse u^{-1}=t^2+t+1 verified by (t-1)(t^2+t+1)=t^3-1=1; powers u^k all have norm 1 (the higher-degree Pell chain).
Norm equation N(xi)=2 solved by xi=t (N(t)=2); the coset t*u^k gives infinitely many solutions in one class mod units (Z[cbrt2] has class number 1).
Classical Pell x^2-2y^2=1 recovered as the rank-1 real-quadratic special case (Brahmagupta chain from (3,2)).
open: Lean formalization of the rank specialization for a concrete cubic (Docker-gated; no build this session).

knownResults.goal: Formalize, for a concrete cubic field (Q(cbrt2)), the unit-group rank and the N(xi)=1 chain via the fundamental unit, plus a general finiteness statement for N(xi)=m solution classes, reusing Mathlib’s Dirichlet unit theorem.

insights: Pell is the signature-(2,0) rank-1 case of Dirichlet; degree>2 raises the unit rank to r1+r2-1, so there can be SEVERAL fundamental units (e.g. totally real cubic x^3-3x-1 has rank 2).
Mixed signature matters independent of degree: Q(cbrt2) is degree 3 yet still rank 1 (signature (1,1)) — one complex place. Rank, not degree, controls the number of fundamental units.
The field norm is most cleanly defined (and Lean-formalizable) as det of multiplication-by-xi on an integral basis; for Q(cbrt2) this yields a^3+2b^3+4c^3-6abc.
For Q(cbrt2) the fundamental unit is t-1, with explicit inverse t^2+t+1 since (t-1)(t^2+t+1)=t^3-1=1 — a concrete, formalizable witness of an O_K^x generator.

N(xi)=m has finitely many solution CLASSES mod units: each class corresponds to an ideal of norm |m| (finitely many), and within a class solutions form one O_K^x-coset (S-unit/class-group finiteness).
